name: org.machanism.machai:genai-client
description: GenAI Client is a Java library in the Machanism ecosystem that provides a provider-neutral API for generative AI and embedding workflows. It resolves provider/model identifiers such as OpenAI:gpt-4o-mini, initializes provider implementations, manages prompts and instructions, executes model requests, and records token usage. Supported integrations include OpenAI-compatible services, Anthropic Claude, EPAM CodeMie, local host-managed Tools, and a no-op None provider. The library supports Java functional tools through ServiceLoader and annotations, optional OpenAI web search and MCP server tools, embedding providers, configuration-driven endpoints and credentials, project-directory context, and usage statistics. It is useful for Java applications implementing AI-assisted workflows, tool orchestration, semantic search, and content generation. The artifact is built for Java 8 bytecode and is published as a Maven library.

usageContext: Applications integrating OpenAI, Anthropic, or CodeMie

constructors.description: Utility manager for resolving and initializing ProcessProvider and EmbeddingProvider implementations dynamically from a provider/model identifier and a Configurator. It is a static utility API; applications normally call its static methods rather than instantiate it.

examples.description: Resolve and initialize a chat provider using a Provider:Model identifier and the application's configured credentials and settings.

features.name: Resolve and initialize a chat provider
features.description: Dynamically loads the provider implementation corresponding to the provider identifier in a Provider:Model string, initializes it with the model and configuration, and returns the ProcessProvider. A blank provider name returns null; an invalid or unavailable provider results in IllegalArgumentException.

examples.description: Select the OpenAI provider and initialize it for gpt-4o-mini using a Configurator containing OPENAI_API_KEY and any optional provider settings.

features.name: Resolve and initialize an embedding provider
features.description: Dynamically loads and initializes an EmbeddingProvider using a Provider:Model identifier or a fully qualified embedding implementation class name. Returns null for a blank provider name and throws IllegalArgumentException when the implementation cannot be resolved or initialized.

examples.description: Initialize an embedding provider for text-embedding-3-small to generate vectors for indexing or semantic retrieval.

features.name: Register and execute Java functional tools
features.signature: public void applyTools(org.machanism.machai.process.provider.ProcessProvider provider, java.lang.String[] tools, java.lang.Class<?> appClass)
features.description: FunctionToolsLoader discovers FunctionTools implementations with Java ServiceLoader, filters by SupportedFor compatibility and optional regular-expression tool-name filters, then registers tool, prompt, and resource declarations with the provider. Implementations can expose public methods using Tool, Param, Prompt, and Resource annotations.

examples.description: After initializing a provider and registering a FunctionTools implementation in META-INF/services/org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools, apply all compatible tools to a real application processor. Use a regular-expression array instead of null to restrict registered callable tools.

features.name: Record and report model token usage
features.description: UsageStatistics stores usage records by model identifier and supports model-specific and aggregate reporting for input, cached input, and output token counts. This supports application diagnostics and consumption reporting.

examples.description: Record a provider usage result under its model identifier, then query the statistics object for model-level or aggregate usage reports.

customizations.name: org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools
customizations.description: Implement this service-provider interface to package custom Java capabilities for discovery and registration with compatible AI providers. Public methods can be marked with Tool, Prompt, and Resource annotations; use SupportedFor to limit a bundle to selected application classes.

examples.description: Create a public tool bundle, provide clear model-facing parameter descriptions, and publish its fully qualified class name in the Java ServiceLoader descriptor. Validate inputs and constrain file, network, or command access in the implementation.

customizations.name: org.machanism.machai.process.provider.ProcessProviderAdapter
customizations.description: Decorate a provider delegate to add application-level behavior such as logging or metrics while preserving the provider lifecycle. The adapter itself does not provide retry behavior.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.process.provider.ProcessProvider
studs.description: Provider-neutral conversational AI contract for initialization, instructions and prompt handling, tools, and model execution. Concrete implementations adapt supported AI services or provide local/no-op behavior.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.process.provider.EmbeddingProvider
studs.description: Provider contract for creating embedding representations from input content. Concrete provider implementations connect the common API to embedding services.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools
studs.description: Service-provider interface that application developers implement to contribute discoverable Java tool, prompt, and resource bundles to the provider lifecycle.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.process.tools.ToolFunction
studs.description: Callback contract for invoking a registered tool with Jackson JSON parameters and optional runtime context objects.

examples.title: Install, configure, and run OpenAI chat with a custom Java tool
examples.description: Add the library to a Maven application, provide the API credential in application configuration, publish a ServiceLoader tool bundle, resolve a provider, and apply the registered capability before executing the application workflow.

steps.content: Declare org.machanism.machai:genai-client:1.4.3 as a dependency in the application's pom.xml. The library is compiled for Java 8 and also depends on provider SDKs and the Machanism Configurator artifact.

Create a Configurator populated with OPENAI_API_KEY from a securely managed environment or secret store. Optionally configure OPENAI_BASE_URL for a compatible endpoint, GENAI_TIMEOUT, MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, and WebSearchTool.type. Do not commit credentials to source control.

Implement org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools, add public methods annotated with @Tool and @Param, and list the implementation class in src/main/resources/META-INF/services/org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools.

Call ProcessProviderManager.getProvider with OpenAI:gpt-4o-mini and the configured Configurator, then call FunctionToolsLoader.applyTools(provider, null, YourApplication.class). Set project-directory context where required and apply input validation and authorization in each tool.

Attach the user's prompt or instructions using the provider API, invoke the provider's perform workflow, and process its response. When the model requests the registered project_summary function, the provider invokes the local method and continues the model interaction with its result.

examples.title: Configure OpenAI web search and MCP tools
examples.description: For an OpenAI provider, optionally configure built-in web search and one or more MCP servers in the same Configurator passed to provider initialization. Set WebSearchTool.type to enable web search; configure sequential MCP groups with a name and valid URL. Store authorization secrets outside source control.

examples.title: Initialize an embedding provider for semantic retrieval
examples.description: Resolve OpenAI:text-embedding-3-small with ProcessProviderManager.getEmbeddingProvider, submit application text through the embedding provider API, and store the resulting vectors in the application's chosen retrieval index for later similarity search.
